message.content:
At 10 kPa (≈ 0.01 MPa) the melting/freezing curve of pure water lies well above the triple‑point pressure (≈ 0.006 MPa).  
Along this curve the temperature drops roughly linearly with decreasing pressure:

| Pressure | Freezing point (°C) |
|----------|---------------------|
| 0.1 MPa  | 0 °C                |
| 0.08 MPa | –2 °C               |
| 0.06 MPa | –5 °C               |
| 0.04 MPa | –9 °C               |
| 0.03 MPa | –12 °C              |
| 0.02 MPa | –16 °C              |
| **0.01 MPa** | **–21 °C**          |

So, for pure water at 10 kPa the equilibrium freezing point is approximately **–21 °C**.  

(If you need a more precise value, consult a detailed phase‑diagram table or a thermodynamic database.)
